articles.title: Tom Brady’s property moves from Boston to Miami: A look at the real estate decisions behind the seven-time champion’s next chapter
articles.summary: Tom Brady no longer owns property in Massachusetts.
articles.body: Tom Brady no longer owns property in Massachusetts. The Brookline mansion he built with Gisele Bündchen sold on Christmas Eve 2020, and his biggest real estate project now sits on Indian Creek Island in Miami. The lot cost $17 million in 2020. In January 2025, Bloomberg reported that the newly finished house had drawn bids above $150 million, though no sale has been confirmed. Between those two addresses sits a story about timing, patience and how a quarterback learned to treat housing as a business.How Tom Brady's property base shifted from Boston to MiamiThe move started well before the quarterback left New England. Brady and Bündchen listed 112 Woodland Road in August 2019 at $39.5 million, then cut the price to $33.9 million two months later. Brady joined the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in March 2020, and the house was still there. It came off the market as COVID-19 hurt luxury sales, then returned quietly as an off-market listing.The deal closed on December 24, 2020. The deed showed a price of $1 and named a trustee as the buyer, who may not have been the final owner. Boston real estate circles believed the property was offered at $32.5 million. Nobody involved has confirmed a number.The Miami purchase landed in the same stretch. Forbes reported that the couple paid $17 million late in 2020 for a tear-down property on Indian Creek Island. Their Manhattan apartment also sold for nearly $37 million around then. Within months, three big holdings became one big plan.A Tampa contract explains why Brady wanted to be in Florida. It does not explain why he picked Miami, which sits across the state. That choice reads like a decision about life after football, not just the next season.Why the Brookline mansion took so long to sellThe house was not a small ask. It was built in 2015 on about five acres beside The Country Club, and it covers 12,112 square feet. Buyers at that price are rare, and the pool shrinks further when a pandemic keeps people at home.Neighbors faced the same wall. Paul Fireman's mansion down the street sold for $23 million in 2020, after it was listed at $90 million in 2016. Against that backdrop, Brady's sale looks less like a failure and more like a reasonable exit. If the reported $32.5 million is right, he came away about 18 percent below his first ask.The private route also made sense. Off-market sales keep prices out of public view, and that protects a seller who has already cut once. Brady lost some money on paper but avoided a public markdown fight, which is a trade many owners at this level choose.What Tom Brady built on Indian Creek IslandIndian Creek is a man-made island with about 40 residences, a country club and its own police department. It is known as the Billionaire Bunker, and Jeff Bezos has bought two homes there.Brady did not keep the original house. The two-acre lot now holds a two-story home with a security building, gym, cabana, pool and sport court, according to property documents. The address is 26 Indian Creek Island Road. Reports differ on timing. Bloomberg called the house newly finished in early 2025, while other outlets date completion to early 2026, so the build clearly ran long.The money behind it is partly visible. The Real Deal reportedly found a $35 million construction loan from Citizens Bank in July 2024. That is a normal way to fund a custom build, even for someone with Brady's income.He also spread his base. He owns a 14,000-square-foot estate in Brentwood, California, that he was renovating, and he set up office space for his family business in Bay Harbor, close to Indian Creek.Is the $150 million Miami house really for sale?Not officially. Bloomberg reported that the property was being shown to a small group of buyers, with no public listing. The $150 million figure came from bids, not a closed deal. Later coverage in 2026 still describes it as a reported price, and I found no confirmed sale or listing.If a deal did close near that number, it would top the $107 million Ken Griffin paid for a Coconut Grove estate in 2022 and set a Miami record. The gap with Brady's costs is also worth noting. A $17 million lot plus a multi-year build does not equal profit. Construction, financing and carrying costs eat into any headline price.What stands out is the pattern. Brady sold high-profile homes quietly, held land through a long build, and tested the market without a listing. Whether he sells or stays, the Miami house is now his main real estate story.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: "Caught me b**ging an NFL head coach": Mike Vrabel scandal follows Dianna Russini as NFL analyst questions her return to the spotlight
articles.summary: Dianna Russini may be preparing to reclaim her place in NFL media, but her reported comeback is already facing criticism.
articles.body: Dianna Russini may be preparing to reclaim her place in NFL media, but her reported comeback is already facing criticism. Months after her departure from The Athletic following controversy surrounding New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel, the former NFL insider appears ready to return to the spotlight. However, not everyone believes the move makes sense. WFAN radio host Gregg Giannotti has openly questioned why Russini would want to return to the same industry, particularly after the controversy damaged her professional standing and brought intense public scrutiny.Gregg Giannotti questions Dianna Russini’s NFL return after Mike Vrabel controversyRussini's reported plans to return to NFL coverage became a talking point after Pro Football Talk revealed on Wednesday that she had started contacting people across the league about her next professional move. According to the report, she told industry contacts that she would be returning to work "next week."The news caught Giannotti's attention during Thursday's episode of Boomer & Gio. Rather than welcoming the possibility of her comeback, the radio personality questioned why Russini would choose to remain in football journalism when other career opportunities were available."Why, in this business? Why not something else? Anything," Giannotti said. "Go work at a hotel. Be the person who fills out the waivers when you go on the banana boat in the Bahamas. Anywhere, just get out of here."He also suggested that familiarity with an industry can make it difficult for someone to consider a fresh start, even when their professional circumstances change.“I think she was trying to think about, ‘How do I get back into the NFL and do all these things that I did in the NFL?’ Just like many people, I don’t think it [change] crosses their minds. This is what I know, and this is what I do, as opposed to taking a risk and trying something different,” added.Giannotti then made his position even clearer with a blunt personal comparison.“I’ll tell you right now. If someone caught me banging an NFL head coach, I’d be out of here,” he said.Dianna Russini’s Mike Vrabel scandal continues to follow her careerRussini resigned from The Athletic on April 14, shortly after Page Six published photographs showing her with Vrabel at a hotel in Sedona, Arizona. Some images showed the two hugging and holding hands, triggering widespread speculation about their relationship.Both figures denied any wrongdoing. Vrabel described the interaction as innocent, while Russini maintained that the photographs did not represent the larger group of six people who had spent time together that day.The controversy did not end with her resignation. A September review by The Athletic examined 903 stories, 77 videos and 204 podcast episodes. It found no clear evidence of bias towards Vrabel's teams but concluded that Russini's undisclosed relationship violated the publication's standards, regardless of whether it was romantic.Meanwhile, her next destination remains uncertain. Front Office Sports reported that Russini was almost certainly the mystery host of a new weekly NFL programme planned by BetUS. The company was expected to reveal its host on Monday.For now, Russini's reported comeback has raised another question: Can she rebuild her career in the same NFL media landscape where the controversy unfolded?Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ $325 million KC Current face another defining moment after stunning NWSL playoff twist
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have another reason to celebrate as the Kansas City Current continue their push for NWSL glory.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have another reason to celebrate as the Kansas City Current continue their push for NWSL glory. The club, which the couple co-owns, delivered a crucial playoff performance at CPKC Stadium, defeating Angel City FC 1-0 after extra time on Saturday. The victory carries special significance for Kansas City after last year's disappointing quarterfinal exit on home soil. This time, the Current found a way through, keeping their championship hopes alive and giving their supporters a memorable moment in front of their home crowd.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes celebrate KC Current's NWSL playoff breakthroughThe Kansas City Current had plenty riding on this quarterfinal clash. Playing at home brought both an advantage and added pressure, especially after their previous postseason campaign ended earlier than expected.Angel City FC arrived in strong form, having gone unbeaten across its previous 10 matches, with eight victories and two draws. The visitors also looked dangerous during the opening stages, creating some of the better scoring opportunities and forcing Kansas City to work hard defensively.However, the Current gradually took control. They struggled to find the finishing touch during the first half, but their attacking intent became increasingly clear as the match progressed.Kansas City finished regulation time with 16 shots compared to Angel City's seven. The home side also produced 10 attempts in the second half alone, putting sustained pressure on the visitors' defence.Despite creating several promising opportunities, the Current could not find a breakthrough during the initial 90 minutes. The match went into extra time, where Kansas City continued to push forward and threatened through multiple corner kicks.KC Current keep championship dreams alive with dramatic extra-time victoryThe decisive moment finally arrived in extra time when Kansas City earned a penalty kick. After spending much of the contest searching for a way past Angel City's stubborn defence, the opportunity gave the home side its chance to settle the contest.The resulting 1-0 victory sent the Current into the NWSL semifinals, turning a tense afternoon into a celebration for the players and supporters.For Patrick and Brittany Mahomes, the result also marks an important moment for their investment in women's professional soccer. The couple joined the ownership group of the Kansas City Current in 2023, alongside other prominent investors, helping strengthen the club's profile.Patrick has built his reputation through his success with the Kansas City Chiefs, but his involvement in the Current reflects a wider interest in the city's sporting future. Brittany has also played an active role in the club's ownership journey.Now, the Current have taken another important step towards the NWSL title. Their quarterfinal victory not only erases last season's disappointment but also puts them closer to delivering another major sporting achievement for Kansas City.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Patriots Trade Rumor: Unexpected Name Could Be on Move at Deadline
articles.summary: The NFL Trade Deadline is rapidly approaching on Tuesday, November 10th. With that, rumors are swirling around how the New England Patriots could be getting...
articles.body:
The NFL Trade Deadline is rapidly approaching on Tuesday, November 10th. With that, rumors are swirling around how the New England Patriots could be getting ready to prepare for their next playoff run.

Most fans think first and foremost about adding players at the deadline. However, there have also been rumors that the Patriots could potentially move on from several players.

The conversation about moving on from Patriots players has largely focused on the defensive side of the ball. Still, the opportunity to move players goes beyond that. Dan Graziano of ESPN even recently shared that the focus could be on quarterback Tommy DeVito.

Could the New England Patriots Move Tommy DeVito?

Luckily, the Patriots haven't had much reason to think about the backup quarterback position this season. Drake Maye has bounced back from his slow start and stayed healthy. So, Tommy DeVito has largely remained on the bench while Behren Morton acts as the team's third-string option.

Other teams around the NFL haven't been so lucky. Injuries abound and several playoff contenders are without a healthy starting quarterback. So, it makes sense to Graziano that the Patriots could get calls about him, and that they'd move him for the right price.

"Quarterback Tommy DeVito," Graziano wrote . "I don't think the Patriots are trading players. However, DeVito is a backup quarterback with NFL starting experience, so it's not wild to think New England could get a call."

DeVito is in his second season with the Patriots. He had previously played for the New York Giants , where he developed a bit of a cult following and did have experience as a starter. In New England, he's played in one game. That was in relief during the blowout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season.

The rumors around the New England Patriots go well beyond DeVito. That includes the idea that they could move a player like Carlton Davis or Christian Barmore from the defense. Then, there's the idea that they could bring in a wide receiver or a running back to help address injury concerns.

Seth Walder of ESPN isn't thinking skill positions. Instead, he thinks if the Patriots add, it will be to the offensive line.

" Saints G Cesar Ruiz ," Walder wrote. "Both of the Patriots' Week 1 starters at guard — Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and Mike Onwenu (ankle) — are on injured reserve. In Ruiz, New England would be adding a starting-caliber guard who is having a particularly good season, with a 78th percentile pass block win rate. He's a better pass protector than run blocker, but the former is more important in New England where protecting Drake Maye is the most important job of the offensive line."

There may be something to that from Walder. The Athletic recently reported that the Patriots shouldn't expect a move at wide receiver or running back. That, of course, leaves room to add on defense or along the offensive line.

Still, there are a couple of days for things to change. The NFL Trade Deadline isn't until 4:00 p.m. EST on Tuesday, November 1oth.
